thread:
Sean Gallagher: Need to lock GA criteria for Runtime LTS this week. What’s the bar where SRE is comfortable saying “yep, this is a real channel” vs pilot forever. Please drop concrete/measurable criteria (patches shipped, incident rate, perf stability, docs/support readiness). I’ll roll up into a checklist.

Rafael Mendes: +1. GA criteria should be objective enough that we can do go/no-go without vibes. I’d propose we require:
- >=2 successful patch releases on the LTS line (same branch) with full gates
- no Sev1 customer incidents attributable to LTS runtime for 30 days post latest patch rollout
- perf gates passing w/out waivers (or waivers are documented + signed off)

Allison Grant: For perf stability, we should define what “stable” means:
- perf-canary suite covers the canonical workloads (short/long, mixed, tool calling-ish, embeddings?) + GPU SKUs
- p95 latency regression threshold <= 3% vs previous LTS patch on those workloads
- throughput regression threshold <= 2% (token/s) on primary GPUs
- flake rate on perf gate jobs < 10% over the last 2 weeks (otherwise we’re playing roulette)

Connor O'Brien: On “successful patch releases”: I’d say 2 is minimum, 3 is better. But we can say “2 shipped + 1 dry-run RC through the full pipeline” as a compromise.
Also: release artifacts must be signed + checksums published + provenance mapping commit -> artifact -> release notes.

Talia Benson: I like making the criteria “GA when X” rather than “we think.” Drafting a list, pls sanity check:
1) Release process proven: 2 consecutive LTS patch releases completed on schedule (monthly cadence), including comms + internal handoff.
2) Backport policy live + followed: at least 5 backports processed using the rubric (security/Sev1/Sev2) w/ approvals recorded.
3) Observability: dashboards + alerts specific to LTS traffic (latency, error rate, OOM, scheduler saturation) are in place.
4) Support readiness: Support playbook done, intake template exists, and on-call/escalation path is tested.

Marcus Reed: Perf suite coverage note: for GA we need baseline + stability numbers for at least:
- A100 80GB + H100 80GB (hosted/dedicated reality)
- L4 or L40S (some private customers)
- Mixed sequence length workload (p50 small, p95 large) bc scheduler regressions hide there.
And: perf gate should compare against last LTS patch, not main.

Sergio Costa: On observability/alerts: I can commit to having the “LTS rollouts” dashboard + alert rules in slo-toolkit before GA.
But we need to define alert ownership during rollout week. Suggest:
- Release Eng owns “release gate failed”
- SRE owns “patch rollout SLO burn” and “customer-facing incident”
Also should require that we can segment traffic by runtime channel (lts vs main) consistently in metrics.

Dev Patel: Support readiness criteria should include:
- KB / playbook in CS+Support space (triage steps, required logs, reproduction template)
- “How to request backport” flow tested end-to-end (ticket -> severity -> eng review -> backport PR -> patch release)
- Customer comms templates reviewed by CS + Legal(?) for security patches
We got burned last year on “we’ll patch soon” language.

Rachel Kim: From CS side: GA means we can confidently tell enterprise “you can sit on this for 6-12 months.” I’d add:
- documented support window (e.g., 12 months) + clear EOL policy
- upgrade + rollback guidance for Private (installer + helm) w/ a validation checklist
- known issues page with workarounds (even if it’s short), so CS has something to point to.

Marissa Cole: Product ask: release notes must be “enterprise grade.” For GA we should require:
- LTS release notes template used for 2 patches
- includes: categorized changes, known issues, upgrade notes, compatibility matrix (runtime<->installer/helm), and CVE format when applicable
- release notes accessible from docs + linkable for AEs/CSMs

Mateo Alvarez: I’m good with a strict bar as long as it doesn’t block on perfection. GA should mean “repeatable + safe.” I’d frame it like:
- process + tooling in place
- rollback story works
- perf + correctness protected by gates
- cross-functional readiness (SRE/Support/CS)
But yes, we need measurable checks.

Hanae Suzuki: Security angle: GA criteria should include vuln response commitments actually being executable:
- out-of-band security patch procedure documented + rehearsed once (tabletop ok)
- SBOM generation (or at least manifest + dependency inventory) attached to artifacts
- signing keys access model approved (no shared creds; audited)

Rafael Mendes: On incidents: “no Sev1 for 30 days” is good but we should clarify scope: attributable to LTS runtime *changes* (kernel/scheduler/runtime), not infra-level incidents.
Maybe:
- 0 Sev1 and <=1 Sev2 attributable to LTS runtime within 30 days after GA candidate patch
- any Sev2 must have RCA + corrective action (test/gate added)

Allison Grant: +1 to scoping. Also: if perf regression triggers a Sev2, that’s basically as bad as a Sev1 for enterprise. So maybe add:
- 0 perf regressions > threshold escaping to customers during pilot
OR
- if it happens, GA blocked until a gate catches it (and we rerun 1 patch cycle)

Connor O'Brien: For release cadence: I’m slightly worried requiring “on schedule monthly” will be brittle with holidays etc.
Alternate: “2 releases within a 6-week window each, with published target date and comms.”
But I agree we should show we can hit cadence.

Sean Gallagher: This is great. Trying to turn into a crisp GA checklist. Current draft:
A) Patch track record
- 2 consecutive LTS patch releases shipped w/ full CI + perf gates + signed artifacts + published slower-change release notes
- 1 additional RC/dry-run through pipeline (optional but preferred)

B) Reliability/incident bar (pilot window)
- 0 Sev1 attributable to LTS runtime changes for 30 days post latest LTS patch rollout
- <=1 Sev2 attributable to LTS runtime changes, w/ RCA + new regression test/perf gate added before GA

C) Perf stability bar
- perf suite covers A100 + H100 + one “private-ish” SKU (L4/L40S)
- p95 latency regression <= 3% vs previous LTS patch on canonical workloads
- throughput regression <= 2% vs previous LTS patch
- perf gate flake rate < 10% (2-week trailing)

D) Observability + rollback
- LTS-specific dashboards + alerting live (SLO burn, error rate, OOM, saturation) + can segment LTS traffic
- documented rollback procedure (Hosted/Dedicated + Private) + tested once in staging

E) Docs + customer-facing readiness
- backport policy published + used for >=5 backports w/ approvals recorded
- known issues + workarounds page exists
- Private upgrade/rollback guide + compatibility matrix (runtime<->installer/helm)
- Support/CS playbook + intake template + comms templates reviewed

Anything missing / any thresholds too strict?

Marcus Reed: Perf thresholds are fine. Only tweak: for some workloads p95 noise can be >3% depending on runner contention. But since this is LTS, strict is ok *if* we enforce runner isolation. Otherwise we’ll be waiving constantly.

Sergio Costa: If we’re going to commit to flake rate <10%, we need dedicated runner capacity for patch week (or an exception process). I’ll note that as an “infra prerequisite.”

Dev Patel: Looks good. I’d add a line: “Support escalation path + on-call rota for LTS patch week is published” (who watches what, when). Otherwise it’s chaos.

Rachel Kim: +1. Also: for GA we should have named pilot accounts that signed off that the cadence + notes are usable. Not a formal requirement, but a checkpoint.

Connor O'Brien: I’m ok with these. One more: version pinning works end-to-end:
- Private installer can pin to exact LTS patch and verify checksums
- Helm values support selecting LTS channel + exposes release notes URL
We should make that explicit under D or E.

Allison Grant: +1. Also: “perf gate uses previous LTS patch baseline” should be written down, otherwise it’ll drift to comparing against main.

Mateo Alvarez: No objections. Let’s ship this as the GA checklist and align in leadership. If runner capacity becomes the only blocker, we’ll staff it.

Sean Gallagher: Cool. I’ll incorporate tweaks (pinning, on-call rota, runner isolation note) and drop into the GA readiness doc + link here for final :thumbsup:.
